Area under the disease progress curve and stairs

Source: R/pathology.R
audpc.Rd

audpc() integrates the disease progress curve with trapezoids (Shaner and Finney 1977); audps() gives the area under the disease progress stairs of Simko and Piepho (2012), which weighs the first and the last assessment as much as the others: AUDPS = AUDPC + (y1 + yn) / 2 * D / (n - 1), with D the time from the first to the last assessment.

Usage

audpc(
  evaluation,
  dates,
  type = c("absolute", "relative", "standardized"),
  ymax = 100
)

audps(
  evaluation,
  dates,
  type = c("absolute", "relative", "standardized"),
  ymax = 100
)

Arguments

evaluation

Disease intensities: a vector (one unit) or a matrix or data frame with one row per unit and one column per assessment.

dates

Times of the assessments (days or Date values), strictly increasing.

type

"absolute", "relative" or "standardized".

ymax

Largest possible intensity (100 for percentages, 1 for proportions, the top of a rating scale).

Value

A numeric vector with one area per unit.

Details

type = "relative" divides the area by the largest possible one, so it lies between 0 and 1: ymax * D for the AUDPC and ymax * D * n / (n - 1) for the AUDPS, whose stairs are n / (n - 1) times as wide as the curve. type = "standardized" divides by the width only and gives the mean intensity over the epidemic, in the units of the assessments. Missing assessments of a unit are skipped (its area then spans its own assessments only).

References

Shaner, G. and Finney, R. E. (1977). The effect of nitrogen fertilization on the expression of slow-mildewing resistance in Knox wheat. Phytopathology 67, 1051-1056.

Simko, I. and Piepho, H.-P. (2012). The area under the disease progress stairs: calculation, advantage, and application. Phytopathology 102, 381-389.

See also

audpc_by_unit() to compute them for every plot of a trial.

Examples

days <- c(7, 14, 21, 28, 35)
sev <- c(1, 4, 12, 30, 52)
audpc(sev, days)
#> [1] 507.5
audps(sev, days)
#> [1] 693
audpc(sev, days, type = "relative")
#> [1] 0.18125
audps(rbind(plot1 = sev, plot2 = sev / 2), days, type = "standardized")
#> plot1 plot2 
#>  19.8   9.9
